issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: The problem statement (problem_statement.md) instructs students to have a final Stock attribute and says this attribute should be initialized to default values in the instance (no-arg) constructor. Later the same problem statement also requires that the same stock attribute be static (shared across all instances) and that certain methods operating on the stock be static. In Java a static final field cannot be initialized in an instance constructor; the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) initializes stock as a static final field at declaration: private static final Stock stock = new Stock(); This is a contradiction in where/how the stock field should be declared and initialized and will confuse or block students implementing the class according to the textual instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: either (A) require an instance (non-static) final Stock and state explicitly that it must be initialized in the no-arg constructor (e.g., private final Stock stock; and this.stock = new Stock(); in the constructor), or (B) require a static final Stock and state that it must be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). Update the textual instructions and the UML so they consistently refer to the same (static or instance) field and show the intended initialization location.

issues.description: Method name for serving queued orders: The problem statement and UML require a method named checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon that attempts to serve queued orders (public void checkOrderReady()). The solution implementation instead provides a method named processOrders() (public void processOrders()) which implements the described behavior. This identifier/name mismatch between the specification and the solution could confuse students about which method name to implement and which signature the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name in the specification and implementation. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (preserving its behavior and signature), or update the problem statement and UML to require processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). Ensure tests and examples use the same method name so students know which name to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement (SealSaloon UML and text) requires a method named checkOrderReady() that processes and serves queued orders. In the solution implementation the same conceptual operation is implemented as a method named processOrders() (declaration: processOrders() in SealSaloon.java) and orderMeal() calls this.processOrders(). Because the problem text, UML and tasks repeatedly mention checkOrderReady(), students may not recognize that processOrders() is the intended implementation and may be confused where to add/override the required behavior or how to call it from orderMeal().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent with the problem statement. Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() and update its caller (replace this.processOrders() with this.checkOrderReady()), or add a public void checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(). Ensure the method signature and visibility remain public void and that all references match the name used in the problem statement and UML.
